after.Presentation: Andre Wells, a 59-year-old man with diabetes and reduced plantar sensation, attends the foot clinic after completing cephalexin for redness around a forefoot ulcer.

Exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Earlier examination
items.value: A 9-by-7-mm ulcer with opaque drainage and surrounding warm, swollen skin.

items.label: Current examination
items.value: A 6-by-4-mm shallow ulcer with red granulation tissue and thin straw-colored fluid. Surrounding skin has the same temperature and color as the opposite foot; no swelling or fluctuance is found. Temperature 36.8 C.

items.label: Surface swab
items.value: Heavy Pseudomonas aeruginosa growth; the report lists ciprofloxacin and gentamicin as susceptible.

after.Task: Which antimicrobial plan is appropriate for Andre Wells at this visit?
Options: Add oral ciprofloxacin to offloading and dressings
Add topical gentamicin to offloading and dressings
after.Explanation: Clinical infection and a positive surface culture are different findings. The current examination and healing trajectory do not establish persistent soft-tissue infection. Continue offloading and dressings; antibiotics should not be prescribed to sterilize an uninfected ulcer or promote its healing. New inflammation or deeper findings would require reassessment.

retainedVersion.status: Unchanged historical draft; included to explain parking, not submitted as a round-five candidate.

independentReview.title: Foot ulcer follow-up

cues.why: The key is the sole maintain/no-drug plan beside two Add drug plans. This structural outlier is easy to pair with the conspicuously improving examination; it is a cue risk, although option structure alone does not prove the answer.

cues.phrase: Surrounding skin has the same temperature and color as the opposite foot; no swelling or fluctuance is found. Temperature 36.8 C.
cues.why: Together with the visibly smaller ulcer, this supplies a dense all-clear pattern. A nonmedical reader can favor maintaining care over adding either drug. These observations are legitimate clinical evidence and must not simply be deleted to make the question harder.

cues.phrase: Which antimicrobial plan is appropriate for Andre Wells at this visit?
cues.why: The lead-in frames the answers as antimicrobial plans, but the key names wound care without explicitly stating the antimicrobial decision. This is a category/wording mismatch, not a reliable cue toward the key.

fairness: Node node.n3.foot-culture-versus-clinical-infection.v1: maintaining wound care without additional antimicrobial treatment is the single best offered answer on the supplied current examination. Heavy growth from a surface swab does not by itself establish ongoing infection.

The smaller shallow granulating wound, changed drainage and absence of current surrounding inflammatory findings support clinical improvement despite the surface susceptibility report. Reduced sensation means absence of pain would not be decisive; the item appropriately supplies examination findings instead.

Oral ciprofloxacin and topical gentamicin both represent treatment of the swab rather than a demonstrated current infection. Neither has an equally defensible indication in the visible record. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; this conclusion does not exclude every possible deep complication outside the described case.

The culture-versus-examination conflict is useful, but the current version collapses to the familiar rule not to treat a clinically uninfected ulcer. The two drug alternatives repeat the same basic error. Reading improvement and then choosing no antibiotic does not require two independently consequential decisions at PGY-2/3 level.
No diagnosis label, explanatory option rationale, convergence pattern or absolute uniquely selects the key. The problem is mainly low discrimination and answer-category asymmetry, not an unsafe key.
suggestions: Use a neutral complete lead-in about the next wound-treatment plan and give every option an explicit antimicrobial disposition while keeping offloading and dressings common to all choices.

To meet the requested resident target, introduce a supported specimen-quality or clinical-reassessment decision that actually changes the next action, with a credible competing plan rather than two routes of unnecessary antibiotic use. Supply the observations that resolve that decision and independently review the new objective.

If the intended objective remains this straightforward stewardship boundary, request explicit acceptance as a foundational item rather than claiming moderate difficulty or two consequential steps. Do not hide the current examination to manufacture uncertainty.

parkedItems.originalObjective: Reconcile the current wound examination with a positive superficial culture before prescribing another antimicrobial.
parkedItems.supportedBoundary: The recorded facts support clinical recognition of infection and withholding antibiotics from a clinically uninfected ulcer. The separate deep-infection claim supports recognition and external escalation, not a ranking of sampling techniques or source-control pathways.
reviewResponse: Agree that the improving examination plus two unnecessary-drug alternatives makes the retained v4 easy. Oral and topical treatment repeat the same culture-driven error.
A neutral next-wound-treatment task and explicit antimicrobial dispositions in every option would repair the category mismatch. They would not add a second inference.
Do not delete the current examination, add equivocal redness without resolving its cause, or repackage the old deep-abscess item. Review 2 already found that construction easy with weak competitors.

prospectiveConstruction.stepA: Interpret current inflammatory findings and the provenance of the reported organism to decide whether infection is established and whether the result represents the tissue whose treatment is being considered.
prospectiveConstruction.stepB: If infection is established, choose the appropriate next reassessment/specimen plan rather than automatically prescribing from the surface report.
prospectiveConstruction.closestCompetitor: Act on a plausible organism and susceptibility report immediately rather than resolve whether the specimen represents the current process.
prospectiveConstruction.decidingObservationNeeded: A clinically meaningful current infection assessment plus the actual sampling site and method, with findings that resolve a soft-tissue versus deeper sampling question.
prospectiveConstruction.ablation: In v4, deleting the present examination removes the basis for withholding antibiotics. Adding specimen provenance without changing the treatment question merely reinforces the same no-antibiotic rule.
prospectiveConstruction.counterfactual: New local inflammatory findings would require reassessment under the existing recognition claim. They do not, by themselves, make the offered ciprofloxacin correct or establish which new specimen to obtain.
prospectiveConstruction.status: Considered outline only; no invented resolving observations, proposed key or executable variant.

after.Presentation: Natalie Stone, a 31-year-old woman, attends the breast clinic after drainage of an MRSA abscess. Her infant is healthy and was born at term. A lactation clinician observes feeding and expression from the affected breast.

Exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Wound and latch
items.value: The draining opening lies above the areola beneath a dressing. During the observed latch the infant's mouth remains below the dressing; the dressing stays adherent around the opening.

items.label: Pump contact
items.value: With the flange in position, its upper rim crosses the opening and lifts the dressing edge. Drainage from the opening reaches the flange's inner breast-contact surface and runs toward the milk tunnel.

items.label: Collection path
items.value: The tunnel and bottle remain connected to that flange throughout expression.

after.Task: Which affected-side plan should Natalie Stone follow for the next feed using the observed arrangements?
Options: **KEY:** Breastfeed directly and discard expressed milk
Breastfeed directly and give expressed milk
Pause breastfeeding and give expressed milk
Pause breastfeeding and discard expressed milk
after.Explanation: Apply the contact precaution to each route. The observed latch avoids the covered opening; the pump setup contacts drainage along a component connected to the milk tunnel. Continue the observed direct feed and discard milk from that expression setup. Reassess or change the expression arrangement before collecting milk for use; the decision does not establish that every future pump setup is unsafe.

retainedVersion.status: Unchanged historical draft; included to explain parking, not submitted as a round-five candidate.

independentReview.title: Feeding after drainage

cues.phrase: the infant's mouth remains below the dressing; the dressing stays adherent around the opening
cues.why: This explicitly favorable contact description maps directly to continuing direct feeding. A reader can make the clean-versus-dirty distinction without identifying a clinical mechanism.

cues.phrase: Drainage from the opening reaches the flange's inner breast-contact surface and runs toward the milk tunnel.
cues.why: The visibly dirty collection path maps directly to discarding expressed milk. Combined with the favorable latch description, ordinary contamination reasoning selects the complete key without a second resident-level inference.

cues.phrase: The tunnel and bottle remain connected to that flange throughout expression.
cues.why: This additional linkage reinforces the same contamination answer. It clarifies exposure but adds no independent decision or competing interpretation.

fairness: Node node.n3.lactation-drain-contact-boundary.v1: continuing the observed direct feed and discarding milk collected with the described contaminated setup is the single best offered plan. Healthy term infant status, the covered opening, observed latch and pump contact are supplied.

The complete four-option matrix balances each feed/discard component equally. There is no frequency convergence, uniquely comprehensive option, grammar outlier, diagnosis-to-option lexical match or rhetorical absolute. The shortcut arises from the very explicit clean/contaminated route descriptions, not an unbalanced matrix.

Giving the expressed milk disregards the described wound-drainage exposure; pausing the observed direct feed treats the protected latch as though it had the same contact. Neither alternative is equally supported by this record. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified in the assessed fields.

There are two route judgments, but each applies the same immediately visible contact distinction. Counting them as two consequential reasoning steps overstates the cognitive demand. The unusual setting may require knowledge of MRSA feeding precautions, but the options and exhibit make the answer accessible through common-sense contamination avoidance.

The task is appropriately limited to the observed arrangements and next feed. The verdict does not imply that every future expression setup is unsafe or that every infant shares this patient's circumstances.
suggestions: Keep the complete balanced matrix and necessary contact observations; do not obscure whether drainage reaches the collection path to manufacture difficulty.

For a resident-level revision, test a supported concrete next action after a specified change in wound coverage or equipment contact, so reassessment changes the feeding/collection plan rather than asking two restatements of the same contact rule. State the actual arrangement and keep all options at that same decision stage.

If the exact objective is simply recognizing safe versus contaminated routes, seek explicit foundational/safety-item acceptance and label the difficulty easy. Cosmetic removal of the collection-path sentence will not create a second consequential step.

parkedItems.originalObjective: Apply contact precautions separately to the observed affected-side latch and expression arrangement.
parkedItems.supportedBoundary: The recorded ABM/CDC fact supports continued feeding or expressed milk when mouth and flange avoid infected tissue, drainage and the drain site. The other recorded facts support ultrasound and selected source control; they do not supply a new equipment-decontamination, milk-handling or special-infant protocol.
reviewResponse: Agree that the balanced four-option matrix avoids convergence but still asks two applications of one immediately visible contact rule.
Retain the necessary contact observations. Removing the milk-path linkage would recreate the fairness gap identified in review 2 rather than create clinical difficulty.

Considered the suggested change in coverage or equipment contact: a newly observed protected or exposed arrangement changes permission under the same conditional rule, but this alone is still clean/contaminated matching. It does not meet the requested independent second resident-level decision.

prospectiveConstruction.stepA: Interpret the changed wound coverage and contact path rather than assume that the earlier feeding assessment still applies.
prospectiveConstruction.stepB: Choose a concrete feeding/collection action for the new arrangement, including any consequence for milk collected under a different arrangement.
prospectiveConstruction.closestCompetitor: Carry an earlier feeding permission into a changed arrangement, or treat a correction to future collection as resolving a prior collection exposure.
prospectiveConstruction.decidingObservationNeeded: The sequence of actual contacts would distinguish the arrangements, but it supplies no independent clinical mechanism beyond the existing contact rule.
prospectiveConstruction.ablation: Deleting the change in contact leaves the original direct-feed/expressed-milk mapping. Keeping it adds chronology but still repeats the same safety rule; it does not establish PGY-2/3 demand.
prospectiveConstruction.counterfactual: If the infant mouth newly contacts the infected opening, the earlier direct-feeding permission no longer follows from the recorded precaution. Whether a particular corrected collection setup or special infant circumstance warrants a different concrete protocol needs directly supported guidance.
prospectiveConstruction.status: Considered outline only; no invented resolving observations, proposed key or executable variant.

parkedItems.missingSupport: An independently consequential management objective with a directly verified concrete action. The recorded limitation about an immunocompromised infant does not itself specify that action; no withholding interval, equipment protocol or retrospective milk-disposition rule is supplied by it.
parkedItems.reentryTask: Either obtain explicit manager acceptance of this exact objective as a foundational safety item, or identify and verify a separate clinically relevant decision before authoring another resident-level version. Do not add a special-infant scenario or generic referral key to manufacture difficulty.

selfCheck.coverTheKey: The balanced matrix has no component-frequency cue. Nevertheless, explicit protected latch versus drainage in the collection path makes common-sense contact matching sufficient; disguising those findings would reduce fairness.
selfCheck.sameStage: The retained four plans are at the same next-feed decision stage. A revision must preserve that parallel scope, not mix wound drainage, a test and feeding permission.
selfCheck.twoSteps: NOT MET: two routes, or before/after contact arrangements, are two applications of one precaution. No distinct supported second clinical decision has been established.
selfCheck.difficulty: Retained v4: easy, agreeing with the reviewer. An unfamiliar setting does not establish moderate difficulty.
selfCheck.oneBestAnswer: The retained exact contact arrangement supports the intended route-specific answer under its stated healthy-term-infant scope. A more complex changed-setup or special-infant protocol has no established unique key here.
selfCheck.decidingObservation: The sequence of actual contacts would distinguish the arrangements, but it supplies no independent clinical mechanism beyond the existing contact rule.
selfCheck.counterfactual: If the infant mouth newly contacts the infected opening, the earlier direct-feeding permission no longer follows from the recorded precaution. Whether a particular corrected collection setup or special infant circumstance warrants a different concrete protocol needs directly supported guidance.
selfCheck.closestCompetitor: Carry an earlier feeding permission into a changed arrangement, or treat a correction to future collection as resolving a prior collection exposure.

after.Presentation: Victor Lane, a 65-year-old man, attends the surgical follow-up clinic after retroperitoneal lymph-node dissection. You review the hospital team's initial nutrition decision when new abdominal drainage developed.

Exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Drainage
items.value: Clear before meals resumed; subsequently cloudy white.

items.label: Paired samples
items.value: Fluid triglycerides 780 mg/dL; serum triglycerides 120 mg/dL.

items.label: Intake and examination
items.value: Meals meet the team's energy and protein prescription. No vomiting; passing stool. Abdomen soft. The hospital is monitoring drain volume, weight and electrolytes.

after.Task: Which initial hospital nutrition prescription best fits Victor Lane's record?
Options: **KEY:** Oral feeding with long-chain-fat restriction and medium-chain enrichment
Oral feeding with long-chain triglyceride enrichment
Parenteral feeding with intravenous nutrients and cessation of oral feeds
after.Explanation: Interpret the fluid findings with the operative and meal history: they support postoperative chylous loss rather than a calorie-delivery problem. The selected initial nutrition plan uses long-chain-fat restriction with medium-chain enrichment while preserving energy/protein intake and monitoring fluid, electrolytes and nutrition. PN is reserved for a different feasibility or refractory-course decision. The fictional sample values are not diagnostic cutoffs or an escalation rule.

retainedVersion.status: Unchanged historical draft; included to explain parking, not submitted as a round-five candidate.

independentReview.title: Postoperative nutrition review

cues.phrase: Meals meet the team's energy and protein prescription. No vomiting; passing stool. Abdomen soft.
cues.why: This bundles a statement that intake goals are met with reassuring gut-function findings. It steers away from both nutritional enrichment for inadequate intake and parenteral feeding, leaving the composition-changing option. Gut feasibility is legitimate information, but the cluster makes the option set easier without resolving loss severity.

cues.phrase: Oral feeding with long-chain-fat restriction and medium-chain enrichment
cues.why: The key is the only oral prescription with two coordinated composition changes and the only mention of medium-chain fat; its oral competitor merely enriches long-chain triglycerides. This is a weak specificity/novelty cue, not a conclusive nonmedical shortcut. The parenteral option is similarly long, so this is not a uniquely-long-key finding.

fairness: Node node.n3.chyle-leak-diet-composition-versus-calories.v1: the operation, meal-associated white drainage and markedly triglyceride-rich fluid strongly favor chylous loss. Long-chain-fat restriction with medium-chain enrichment is the likely intended initial oral plan; long-chain enrichment is not a close credible competitor once that process is recognized.

The cognitive demand is predominantly recognition of a classic postoperative pattern followed by recall of its familiar dietary association. The paired serum value does not create an additional management decision, and the current long-chain-enrichment distractor does little to distinguish PGY-2/3 reasoning. Two sequential recalls are not two consequential steps under the owner standard.

Single-best-answer confidence is limited against the parenteral option: actual drain output, loss trajectory and resulting volume/nutritional consequences are absent. Saying the hospital is monitoring these variables supplies no results. Adequate oral calories and a functioning gut do not alone establish that continued intestinal fat absorption is appropriate for every severity of chylous loss.

Clinical uncertainty, not a declared factual error: I cannot certify from this offline record that PN is equally appropriate in this particular patient, nor that the intended oral prescription is wrong. The missing severity information prevents confidently dismissing PN across reasonable interpretations of the case. A clinician should establish the supported initial-treatment boundary; no numeric cutoff is inferred here.

The historical hospital decision is clearly distinguished from the current clinic visit. The task is complete. No visible label names chyle, no rhetorical absolute dictates treatment, and the options do not form a majority-component convergence that uniquely selects the key. Difficulty is easy for the apparent intended solution; uncertainty about PN is a fairness defect, not desirable hardness.
suggestions: Supply the actual loss course and relevant physiological/nutritional observations needed to distinguish an initial oral trial from bowel rest/PN, with clinician-supported interpretation. Do not substitute a new unsupported volume threshold or the conclusion mild leak for those observations.

Replace long-chain enrichment with a genuinely credible competing nutrition prescription at the same stage, supported by the clinical objective. Keep option specificity comparable and avoid making only the key a detailed combined prescription.

Make a documented response or meaningful constraint change which plausible nutrition plan is best; otherwise treat the diagnosis-to-diet association as foundational. Preserve the distinction between recognizing chyle and deciding the appropriate route/intensity of nutritional support.
Re-review both single-key fairness and two-step demand after revision. Do not resolve the PN ambiguity solely by asserting in post-answer feedback that it is reserved for another stage.

parkedItems.originalObjective: Recognize the postoperative fluid pattern and select long-chain-fat restriction with medium-chain enrichment rather than increase long-chain fat or start PN.
parkedItems.supportedBoundary: Recorded facts support fluid analysis, monitored initial conservative management and general oral/enteral versus PN boundaries. They explicitly retain heterogeneous evidence and do not define a chyle-loss volume, response duration or physiological threshold that selects PN or invasive escalation.
reviewResponse: Agree that classic fluid recognition followed by the familiar diet association is predominantly recall, and long-chain-fat enrichment is not a credible nearest competitor.

Agree that adequate oral calories and a functioning gut do not resolve the competing PN option without actual loss course and physiological consequences. The retained v4 is not certified single-best against PN.

Considered a real intake/output and nutritional-response record. A falling-output/return-to-earlier-formula sequence would repeat the lay trend-matching shortcut criticized in review 2. A detailed loss record would require a supported interpretation before it could fairly choose oral, enteral or PN treatment.

prospectiveConstruction.stepA: Interpret actual drain-loss trajectory together with nutritional intake, volume status and laboratory course, rather than infer treatment adequacy from fluid appearance or calorie prescription.
prospectiveConstruction.stepB: Use that interpretation to choose the next nutrition route/intensity among credible conservative enteral and PN strategies.
prospectiveConstruction.closestCompetitor: Start PN for ongoing losses despite a functioning gut, or continue a dietary plan because prescribed calories are adequate despite an adverse physiological course.
prospectiveConstruction.decidingObservationNeeded: A documented response or constraint that a permitted source directly supports as distinguishing the offered nutrition plans. Neither a fictional output number nor the phrase being monitored establishes that boundary.
prospectiveConstruction.ablation: Without the loss and physiological course, PN cannot be reliably ranked in the proposed closer option set. With a simple A-better/B-worse table, the answer follows from the trend without the intended clinical reasoning.
prospectiveConstruction.counterfactual: General recorded guidance supports PN when oral and enteral routes are infeasible, contraindicated or insufficient. It does not say which particular course of chylous losses establishes those conditions, or when to abandon a given dietary trial.
prospectiveConstruction.status: Considered outline only; no invented resolving observations, proposed key or executable variant.

parkedItems.missingSupport: A directly supported and clinically reviewed interpretation of a specified postoperative chyle-loss/response course that ranks the closest oral/enteral versus bowel-rest/PN plans. The generic PN boundary and permission to monitor do not establish that exact application. No universal numeric cutoff is inferred.
parkedItems.reentryTask: Verify a bounded initial-versus-refractory nutritional-management decision with permitted guidance and clinician review before constructing the resolving observations. The earlier owner-approved large symptomatic inpatient case does not approve a new stable low-output or PN-escalation variant.

selfCheck.coverTheKey: NOT MET: the key is the only detailed oral composition change; the long-chain-enrichment rival is weak. Reassuring intake/gut statements steer away from PN without settling loss severity.
selfCheck.sameStage: A future revision should compare similarly specified nutrition prescriptions at the same treatment point. Do not mix a generic diet, lymphatic intervention and a loosely defined admission decision.
selfCheck.twoSteps: NOT MET: the retained construction is classic pattern recognition plus diet recall. A loss-response interpretation could change a real second management decision, but that boundary is unverified.
selfCheck.difficulty: Retained v4: easy for the intended answer; unresolved PN ranking is a fairness defect, not difficulty.
selfCheck.oneBestAnswer: NOT ESTABLISHED against PN in v4 because the severity/response context is absent. No replacement key is emitted until that comparison is supported.
selfCheck.decidingObservation: A documented response or constraint that a permitted source directly supports as distinguishing the offered nutrition plans. Neither a fictional output number nor the phrase being monitored establishes that boundary.
selfCheck.counterfactual: General recorded guidance supports PN when oral and enteral routes are infeasible, contraindicated or insufficient. It does not say which particular course of chylous losses establishes those conditions, or when to abandon a given dietary trial.
selfCheck.closestCompetitor: Start PN for ongoing losses despite a functioning gut, or continue a dietary plan because prescribed calories are adequate despite an adverse physiological course.
